title: Operating Lines of Credit — The Association's Own Borrowing Base on a Delivered Certificate
content:
On the Operating Lines of Credit, the borrowing base that stands on a borrowing base certificate is the association's own figure, not the member's.

## Rule

The association works out its own borrowing base for a borrowing base certificate the member has delivered on a line in active or suspended status, and records it on that certificate in place of any figure the member worked out. The figure rests on the collateral values stated on the line's most recent certificate, the one with the latest as-of date. The recording is due whenever a delivered certificate still carries a figure the association has not worked out itself.

## Business effect

Once recorded, the certificate lists the association's amount as its borrowing base wherever the line's certificates are looked up. The stated collateral values, the as-of date, the received date and the way the certificate was delivered stay as they were. Only the borrowing base figure changes.

## Platform reference: `record_certificate_borrowing_base_37c8bf27`

**Capability.** Records the association's own borrowing base on a borrowing base certificate the member has already delivered for an operating line, replacing the figure the certificate carried with the amount supplied.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the servicing representative unlocks `record_certificate_borrowing_base_37c8bf27` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate_id` | Reference number of the delivered borrowing base certificate whose borrowing base is being recorded, as shown when the line's certificates are looked up | Identifier |
| `line_id` | Loan number of the operating line the certificate supports, as shown when the member's operating lines are looked up | Identifier |
| `borrowing_base_amount` | The borrowing base to stand on the certificate; it replaces whatever figure the certificate carried | USD, positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to cents before it is passed |

**Return.** A receipt rendered as text with `certificate_id` (the certificate updated), `line_id` (the line it supports), `borrowing_base_amount` (the USD amount, 2 decimal places, now recorded on the certificate) and `status`, the literal "recorded", meaning the certificate now carries this borrowing base.

## Contract questions

**Does the call change the collateral values on the certificate?** No. It leaves the stated values, the as-of date, the received date and the delivery channel untouched.

**Which certificate does the amount go on?** The certificate named by `certificate_id`; the amount stands as that certificate's borrowing base from then on.
